title: Reject the unchanged spool UTF-8 SIMD wrapper
question: Does a safe SIMD wrapper reduce complete-Run cost while preserving strict errors?
summary: Both opposite-order pipeline pairs miss the frozen benefit rule; the wrapper and dependency change were reverted.

workloads: One million plain probe-v1 rows; partition -> probabilistic allocation -> child uniform shuffle; four workers and 32-MiB job/shared limits.

validation.summary: Six complete jobs preserve fields, IDs, groups, caps, CSV/Analysis parity and cleanup; recorded Linux/Windows local workflows cover their actual builds.

limitations: Small development cells and uncontrolled cache/background state do not establish general device, shape or tail performance.
Historical percentage gains are not additive; every comparison uses its own pinned baseline.
Sampled UTF-8 CPU share did not isolate spool callers.
Success on these checks does not show SIMD is unhelpful for every workload.
exclusions: Unreplicated ordered control is not pooled with pipeline samples.
Component scans, old timing samples and coarse CPU counters are not independent speed evidence.
reopen_when: A different named cost or materially different, justified integration is required; do not retune or relabel the unchanged rejected wrapper.
